authentication.session: The API returns token. Requests send Authorization: Bearer <token>.
authentication.google: POST /auth/google accepts { credential }, verifies the Google Identity Services ID token, links/creates the account and returns { token, userId, isAdmin }.
authentication.demo: POST /auth/demo issues a non-admin demo session only when DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED=true; the frontend uses it after Google sign-in fails.
authentication.registration: POST /auth/register creates the account but does not issue a token. The frontend signs in with POST /auth/login after registration.
authentication.admin: Admin endpoints enforce the API admin role. Client-side UI is not an authorization boundary.

compose.google_oauth_javascript_origin: Add http://localhost:3000 to the Google OAuth web client's Authorized JavaScript origins.

rules: Each event admission batch is capped at 15 passes per 10-second interval by default and also limited to uncommitted available inventory.
Queue grants are expiring and single-use; seat inventory, reservation state, payment status and admin permissions are server authoritative.
Human-likelihood scores are coarse heuristics for weighted random selection, not definitive bot detection. The public operations endpoint returns aggregate-only data.

The k6 cohort simulation sends traffic only to a dedicated local event and removes its synthetic accounts/event after storing aggregate results. Web-triggered runs are disabled unless explicitly enabled and are authenticated, bounded, and rate limited.
Raw browser cookies, JWTs, and session secrets are never exposed in live operations or simulation reports.
Set both NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY and enable TURNSTILE_REQUIRED=true to enforce Cloudflare Turnstile at queue entry.
Redis and PostgreSQL are started by the supplied Docker Compose stack; their availability is required for API routes.
The frontend has no live payment provider and collects no card or banking credentials.
